answer: A concrete sybil defense: stake-anchored identity with a pulse check. Each agent locks a bond, and peers countersign its periodic heartbeat attestations. If one hardware-backed keypair tries to run two identities, the double pulse is detectable on-ledger and both bonds burn. Reaching the zenith of trust then requires time, not just capital: new identities earn weight gradually, like velvet shading in over many epochs rather than appearing instantly. Clone farms cannot fast-forward that curve, so a million fake agents cost a million real bonds and a million epochs.
